ArXiv eess.AS (Audio).title: NAVIQUAL-XR: Finding the Sweet Spot of a Live Music Environment in Augmented Reality
ArXiv eess.AS (Audio).description:
arXiv:2611.28056v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Augmented Reality (AR) enables immersive spatial audio experiences that extend conventional stereo and head-tracked listening to six degrees-of-freedom (6-DoF) navigation. However, evaluating listener Quality of Experience (QoE) remains a key challenge due to the real-time and dynamic adaptations of the content in AR environments. To address this challenge, we propose NAVIQUAL-XR, an objective model to find the "sweet spot" in AR live music environments validated by subjective tests. ArXiv eess.AS (Audio).title: Granary-v2: Scalable Multilingual Speech Data Curation for Predictable and Controllable Model Outputs
ArXiv eess.AS (Audio).description:
arXiv:2611.28248v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Speech-language models that follow instructions need training data that connects the same recording to different output forms and tasks. We present Granary-v2, a multilingual speech dataset and reusable curation system that provides a data foundation for these models. Granary-v2 extends Granary-v1 with aligned transcript variants and instruction-target pairs for multi-task speech-language training. Language coverage increases from 25 to 48 languages. ArXiv eess.AS (Audio).title: Preserving Prosody in Speaker Anonymization
ArXiv eess.AS (Audio).description:
arXiv:2611.28290v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Effective prosody modeling is essential in natural speech generation applications, but complications arise in speaker anonymization, since speaker attributes are present in acoustic correlates of prosody. Our work aims to improve previous reported tradeoffs between effective speaker obfuscation and preservation of prosodic content. To this end, we integrate an existing pretrained privacy-preserving prosody encoder into a speech synthesis model, enabling prosody-preserving speaker anonymization. ArXiv eess.AS (Audio).title: Speech Emotion Recognition Across Languages: Prosodic Patterns and Self-Supervised Learning
ArXiv eess.AS (Audio).description:
arXiv:2611.29040v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: This study investigates the prosodic patterns of emotional speech across Chinese (CN), German (DE), and English (EN), with a focus on acoustic characteristics. Using ANOVA and mixed-effects modeling, we reveal cross-linguistic and emotion-specific prosodic patterns. ArXiv eess.AS (Audio).title: Voice Agents: From Auditory Intelligence to Auditory Agency
ArXiv eess.AS (Audio).description:
arXiv:2611.29465v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Voice systems increasingly combine streaming speech, persistent state, reasoning, tool use, and embodied control. Once these functions share a runtime, spoken input can change digital or physical state, and recognition or response quality alone no longer characterizes the system. ArXiv eess.AS (Audio).title: S$2$SCORE: A Textless Unified Evaluation Metric for Speech-to-Speech Translation Systems
ArXiv eess.AS (Audio).description:
arXiv:2611.29557v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Evaluating speech-to-speech translation (S$2$ST) systems requires assessing multiple dimensions of translated speech, including semantic adequacy, speaker similarity, and acoustic naturalness. Existing approaches are largely text-based, relying on ASR transcripts and primarily assessing semantic adequacy, while other dimensions require separate metrics. We propose S$2$SCORE, a unified text-free evaluation framework that jointly models these dimensions within a multi-task architecture and produces a human-calibrated overall quality score. S$2$SCO

ArXiv eess.AS (Audio).description:
arXiv:2611.29865v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Self-supervised learning (SSL) encoders are the dominant front end for speech deepfake detection, and the prevailing recipe fine-tunes the full encoder on a small spoofing corpus, maximizing in-domain accuracy at the cost of known degradation under domain shift. Taking a recent cross-attention fusion of SSL and constant-Q cepstral features as a fixed reference recipe, we freeze its encoder and ask which encoder and which backend behave best across domains. ArXiv eess.AS (Audio).title: Which Layer to Trust? Layer Selection in Frozen Speech Encoders for Singing-Voice Deepfake Detection under Signal Corruption
ArXiv eess.AS (Audio).description:
arXiv:2611.29871v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Frozen self-supervised speech encoders have been frequently used for audio deepfake detection. However, the layers are usually chosen from a development set. We examine this choice for singing-voice deepfake detection on CtrSVDD. We train one detection head per layer, plus a learned layer mix, on frozen XEUS (3-4 seeds) and XLS-R (2 seeds). ArXiv eess.AS (Audio).title: BiSAT: Bidirectionally Aligned Semantic-Acoustic Tokenization for Speech Language Models
ArXiv eess.AS (Audio).description:
arXiv:2611.30723v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Speech language models (LMs) generate speech as sequences of discrete tokens. Their tokenizer must therefore preserve both acoustic detail and linguistic content at a low bitrate. Semantic-enhanced tokenizers may lose acoustic detail, whereas acoustic-oriented tokenizers retain acoustic variation that makes language modeling harder. ArXiv eess.AS (Audio).title: SpeechSplice: Pronunciation Control in Encoder-Decoder LLM-based TTS by Replacing Encoder Hidden States
ArXiv eess.AS (Audio).description:
arXiv:2611.30927v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Most large language model (LLM)-based text-to-speech (TTS) methods offer no explicit function for correcting pronunciation. Consequently, these systems frequently mispronounce many everyday words, such as proper nouns, heteronyms, numerals, and domain-specific terms. While weight-editing or fine-tuning can mitigate this, these solutions risk quality degradation and must operate offline. ArXiv eess.AS (Audio).description:
arXiv:2611.28020v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: Extended reality (XR) systems increasingly rely on audio cues to help users locate, interpret, and interact with virtual content, especially when the content is outside the field of view. To support this, many systems use head-related transfer functions (HRTFs) to approximate real-world acoustics. However, a realistic simulation is only one possible presentation. ArXiv eess.AS (Audio).description:
arXiv:2611.28026v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: Most of what matters in a day is spoken and written down nowhere: a dosing interval named at a clinic, a deadline moved in passing, the place a document was set down. Such information is consequential because it is operational, and fragile because it arrives during divided attention -- the moment its importance becomes clear is rarely the moment it was said. arXiv:2611.29315v1 Announce Type: cross

ArXiv eess.AS (Audio).description:
arXiv:2611.30714v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: Video-to-audio generation synthesizes sound that matches a video in content and timing, with applications ranging from film post-production to live streaming, games and interactive world models. Interactive applications receive video continuously and need the sound to follow it in real time, yet most existing video-to-audio models are bidirectional and must observe an entire clip before producing any sound. ArXiv eess.AS (Audio).title: Lightweight Detection and Model Attribution of Synthetic Speech via Residual Statistical Fingerprints
ArXiv eess.AS (Audio).description:
arXiv:2411.14013v5 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: As speech generation technologies advance, so do risks of impersonation, misinformation, and spoofing. We present a lightweight, training-free method for synthetic speech detection and source model attribution. Our method builds on model-specific fingerprints that are computed as the average of the differences between audio signals and their filtered versions, referred to as residuals. ArXiv cs.SD (Sound).title: PopMelodyGen: A Copyright-Aware Platform for Controllable Pop-Melody Generation
ArXiv cs.SD (Sound).description:
arXiv:2611.28686v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Large-scale redistributable symbolic pop-melody data remain scarce due to copyright restrictions, creating a bottleneck for both practical deployment and reproducible research in music generation. We present PopMelodyGen, a copyright-aware platform for controllable pop-melody generation that combines rule-based synthesis with neural generation. Our approach first uses an expert synthesizer to produce large-scale labeled synthetic melodies from explicit musical knowledge and templates, providing scalable pretraining data with auditable provenance

ArXiv cs.SD (Sound).description:
arXiv:2611.28718v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Speech deepfake detectors make few errors on standard benchmarks, yet a simple attack defeats them: the attacker passes fake speech through one short filter, tuned against the detector, and many fakes then pass as real. Training with random filters does not stop this attack, because the attacker uses the worst filter, not a random one.

ArXiv cs.SD (Sound).description:
arXiv:2611.28765v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Symbolic music generation often continues MIDI passages by predicting subsequent notes or events. Held-out prediction loss can overestimate generalization to unseen compositions when training contains another performance or arrangement of a test work. We introduce Multi-View Alignment-Aware Same-Work Identification, combining complementary musical representations with temporal alignment of shared passages to remove test-work versions from training while preserving unrelated material and fixing evaluation files. ArXiv cs.SD (Sound).description:
arXiv:2611.28863v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Voice anonymization aims to conceal speaker identity while preserving linguistic and paralinguistic information. However, certain applications also require the ability to attribute anonymized recordings to their original speakers. Existing recovery approaches often rely on specially designed reversible anonymization systems, limiting their applicability to different anonymization architectures. ArXiv cs.SD (Sound).description:
arXiv:2611.29012v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Spatial audio large language models increasingly combine general audio understanding with spatial perception. Yet overlapping conversations require more than locating speakers. A model must also recover what each person says and match the words to their positions. We examine this challenge in MiDashengLM-Spatial, a binaural model designed for both spatial reasoning and general audio understanding. ArXiv cs.SD (Sound).description:
arXiv:2611.29085v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Partially spoofed audio embeds spoofed segments in a bonafide utterance, and spoof localization is the task of locating them. Most countermeasures (CMs) operate at the frame level. Typically, they include a front-end representing the audio as frames and a back-end classifying each frame as bonafide or spoof. ArXiv cs.SD (Sound).description:
arXiv:2611.29225v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Music creation is inherently iterative, yet many symbolic generation systems still center on producing or regenerating isolated outputs. We present IteraSong, an interactive web-based Digital Audio Workstation (DAW) for LLM-guided iterative symbolic music creation. Unlike one-shot generation systems, IteraSong supports a generate-audition-edit-refine loop over a persistent multi-track project. ArXiv cs.SD (Sound).description:
arXiv:2611.29226v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Autoregressive text-to-speech (TTS) with continuous speech latents avoids quantization-induced information loss, but typically relies on a latent space that is learned separately and then frozen before language-model training. Such a space must satisfy two competing requirements: it must retain enough acoustic detail for high-fidelity reconstruction, yet be sufficiently structured and regularized to support autoregressive prediction by a language model. ArXiv cs.SD (Sound).description:
arXiv:2611.29283v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Adding a singing voice to an existing piano recording requires decisions about melody, syllable placement, pronunciation, timing, and vocal register. ARRANGE organizes this work as a sequence of agent skills with readable intermediate artifacts and composer approval checkpoints. An LLM translates instructions in plain English, notes played on a keyboard, and vocal references into local edits; deterministic scripts validate and apply those edits before open audio models render the result. ArXiv cs.SD (Sound).description:
arXiv:2611.29375v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Audio large language models (LLMs) are typically evaluated on song genre, mood, and instrumentation. A more basic skill is telling whether two short clips play the same melody, chord or instrument. We introduce MusicListenBench, a benchmark of paired listening tests for melody, harmony, timbre, and tempo. Each test item comes with two variants. A FLIP variant changes the music, so the answer must change. A STAY variant changes only the sound, such as room echo or hiss, so the answer must stay the same. ArXiv cs.SD (Sound).description:
arXiv:2611.29411v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: When two musicians in an ensemble play the same instrument, they sound alike and their instruments look alike. Audio-only separators, and audio-visual separators that rely on appearance, cannot tell them apart. What still differs is how each player moves, and when. We study same-instrument per-player separation: a user clicks one musician in a video and receives that musician's sound alone, even when other players in the video play the same instrument. ArXiv cs.SD (Sound).description:
arXiv:2611.29475v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Musical style, a global attribute that functions throughout a whole piece, is a lever widely used by users in modern large music generation models. Yet how style is represented inside these models, and which components drive it, remains largely unexplored. In language models, circuit analysis traces a representation to a sparse sub-network of a few key components, namely attention heads and MLP neurons, and has been used successfully to explain and control global attributes such as emotion. ArXiv cs.SD (Sound).description:
arXiv:2611.29985v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Flow-matching text-to-speech (TTS) models learn how native speakers realize a text, yet this knowledge is used only for synthesis. We show that a frozen TTS model can score non-native (L2) pronunciation without generating audio. For a learner utterance, we compare the model's velocity-prediction error under the target text with its error under a counterfactual text (dropped or swapped) on the same noised input; the difference behaves like a generative goodness-of-pronunciation score. ArXiv cs.SD (Sound).description:
arXiv:2611.30049v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: AIRPiano aims to bring sound to the common practice of rehearsing piano music on a tabletop. Guided by a known score, users make piano-like finger movements on a flat surface without reproducing absolute keyboard positions. The score supplies pitches, while hand motion determines which score events to play and when. We formulate this interaction as online alignment between tabletop hand motion and symbolic score events. CDM — Create Digital Music.description:

First seen on CDM in 2014, version 2 of Taika Systems' instrument adds AUv3 support on iOS -- and parameters modeling predators, hunger, and fear. The result is lush, nuanced layers of sound, pads to leads, that feels uniquely alive.

CDM — Create Digital Music.title: Berlin’s largest electronic music venue, now a stage for debuting military AI
CDM — Create Digital Music.description:
Berlin Kraftwerk, the former power plant in Berlin Mitte associated with Tresor and Ohm, was the venue last week for Helsing's launch of new agentic technology, Clarity. This platform uses the same controversial AI-driven approach implicated in accelerating the use of flawed intelligence and killing civilians in Palestine, Lebanon, and Iran. Kraftwerk's Head of Sales has taken sole responsibility and apologized. But the fiasco seems emblematic of Berlin's pivot from cultural capital to military-industrial capital, with the money that follows.
